evals.name: external-database
evals.prompt: Review the supplied controller and deployment excerpts for reachable correctness and isolation defects. Treat the excerpts as incomplete and distinguish proven paths from missing configuration.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-backed allocation, deletion, readiness and RBAC findings with bounded concurrency claims.
assertions: Finds repeated paid allocation, including crash after creation but before status persistence.
Finds ignored cleanup failure and removal of foreign finalizers; notes missing persisted cleanup protection in the shown path without assuming unseen code.
Finds premature Ready and effective wildcard RBAC through the supplied binding.
Explains replica/rollout side-effect risk without claiming an observed split-brain incident.
Cites file/line evidence and does not claim compilation, deployment or runtime success.

evals.name: helm-architecture
evals.prompt: Review only the supplied architecture contract. Identify applicable obligations and what cannot be established from these artifacts.
evals.expected_output: Scoped architecture review with explicit implementation unknowns and no invented universal framework requirements.
assertions: Does not require Go, OLM, a custom finalizer or a backup feature for the stated contract.
Leaves reconciliation, rendered permissions and runtime correctness unverified.
Treats rolling-update overlap as an open question rather than a proven defect.
Cites contract evidence and does not invent executable tests or implementation behavior.

evals.name: storage-migration
evals.prompt: Review the supplied upgrade procedure against its lossless-upgrade promise. Identify unsafe transitions and the evidence needed to validate a replacement procedure.
evals.expected_output: Semantic-conversion, storage-migration, version-retirement and test-fidelity findings.
assertions: Identifies None conversion as incompatible with the duration-string to integer-seconds change.
Explains that changing storage flags or storedVersions does not rewrite existing objects.
Finds premature retirement of the old API and requires compatibility/migration verification.
Explains why fake-only tests cannot establish API-server upgrade correctness and avoids inventing observed data loss or a version-independent migration API.

evals.name: admission-mutation
evals.prompt: Review both supplied admission implementations against their stated contract. Separate defects in each alternative from verification that requires missing deployment or integration context.
evals.expected_output: MutateA defect, correct bounded assessment of MutateB, and admission-specific verification proposals.
assertions: Finds duplicate sidecar insertion in MutateA on reinvocation or pre-existing sidecar, with invalid-Pod consequences.
Recognizes MutateB as idempotent for the stated insertion contract rather than repeating the MutateA finding against it.
Proposes repeated-application and interaction/final-object tests without assuming webhook ordering or blindly changing failurePolicy.
Cites source lines and keeps TLS, arbitrary webhook composition and live admission results unverified.

evals.name: desired-set-shrink
evals.prompt: Review the supplied reconciliation decision path against the Website API contract, including supported configuration transitions.
evals.expected_output: Stale Ingress exposure finding with safe cleanup and transition-test recommendations.
assertions: Finds that the true-to-false transition leaves the Ingress active while the Website survives.
Explains why owner-reference garbage collection does not implement this transition.
Recommends owner-checked pruning with a true-to-false regression scenario and does not require a custom finalizer for this GC-only fixture.
Cites source lines and does not claim a running cluster or an observed external exposure incident.

evals.name: cache-scale
evals.prompt: Review the supplied cached-client design and scale claim. Verify framework-dependent conclusions against the pinned dependency and separate static conclusions from measurements that have not been supplied.
evals.expected_output: Pinned-source cache-scope finding with bounded memory claims and compatible verification/remediation options.
assertions: Verifies controller-runtime v0.20.4 behavior using pinned primary source evidence.
Identifies on-demand Secret informer creation and broad list/watch/cache scope, rejecting the named-Get retains-only-one claim.
Keeps actual memory, latency and OOM unverified and does not invent bytes-per-object or an authorization breach.
Proposes representative measurement and cache/client choices that preserve authorized cross-namespace references rather than mandating all live reads.

evals.name: event-continuation
evals.prompt: Review the supplied controller decision path and watch wiring against the Widget lifecycle contract. Verify framework-dependent conclusions against the pinned dependency and distinguish static conclusions from unobserved runtime behavior.
evals.expected_output: Evidence-backed event-flow findings for creation, deletion and dependent readiness, with scoped remediation.
assertions: Finds that adding the finalizer then returning leaves initial normal work without a continuing trigger under the stated event contract.
Finds that deletionTimestamp-only updates are filtered and that builder-wide filtering also suppresses dependent status updates needed for readiness.
Verifies pinned controller-runtime v0.20.4 predicate/builder semantics and cites fixture source lines.

Recommends reliable continuation plus event-appropriate filtering, does not treat a single post-finalizer requeue as fixing every path, and does not invent observed cluster behavior or ban all generation predicates.
